summary: Carefully preregistered, well‑executed paired evaluation of a verifier‑guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline for intent→configuration tasks using gpt-5-mini under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The execution artifacts, audit trail, and disclosure (including master-prompt SHA‑256) are present. Results show a very high baseline pass rate (199/200) and a marginal guarded improvement (200/200), with one discordant pair; the manuscript correctly scopes conclusions to the synthetic corpus, single model, and shared_initial_candidate design.
critical_issues: References are not presented as a conventional IEEE numbered bibliography with full bibliographic metadata. The manuscript lists numeric citations in text but the submitted evidence bundle does not show a matching IEEE-style References section with authors, title, venue, year, and DOI/identifier entries; per the track rules, each in-text numbered citation must map to a verified bibliographic record that supports the proximate claim.
required_revisions: Insert a conventional IEEE-formatted References section (numbered entries) for every in-text citation. Each reference must include full bibliographic metadata (authors, title, venue or repository, year, and DOI/identifier where available) and must be verified to support the specific claim(s) for which it is cited. Ensure in-text citation numbers map exactly to the numbered reference list.

Add one brief clarifying sentence in Methods or Results explaining the provider_call_audit counts (model_calls_used = 201 vs completed_episode_count = 400) so readers immediately understand that exactly one shared initial generation was sampled per pair and that the guarded arm reused that same candidate (shared_initial_candidate semantics), with at most one additional repair call producing the extra hosted-model call. Point readers to the archived provider_call_audit for full accounting.
optional_revisions: Consider adding a short table or boxed note (one paragraph) summarizing model-call accounting and how the shared_initial_candidate design reduces hosted-model calls (shared_initial_generation count + repair calls = total model_calls_used) to aid reader comprehension.

In Discussion, expand one sentence to explicitly connect the preregistered power assumptions (baseline 45–65%) to the observed baseline (~99.5%) and note the practical implication that the planned sensitivity was not realized given the unexpectedly high baseline pass rate.
